page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model under the KVM hypervisor. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.e4.large exhibits limited processing and memory capabilities. In stress-ng testing, both single-core (945.88) and multi-core (1857.99) CPU performance fall into the bottom 10% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 164.27 GB/sec, which drops to 14.95 GB/sec for large block uncached reads and 11.46 GB/sec for large block writes, both placing in the bottom 10%. Passmark CPU and memory scores also rank in the bottom 10%, with a database operations score of 558.24 and a Redis SET throughput of 2.53 million operations per second.

Due to its shared CPU allocation and older Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 architecture, the server presents a tradeoff between high memory density and low compute performance. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring a larger memory footprint but minimal CPU utilization. Appropriate workloads include lightweight database caching, basic web serving with low traffic, and non-critical background tasks that do not require sustained high-performance compute or local storage.
